paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Daniel was far from home, with a new name and a new boss. But Daniel "made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s food or wine" (Daniel 1:8). So he went and asked for permission not to.

Now look at HOW he did it. He didn't throw a fit or start a riot. He asked for permission, and then he asked for a ten-day test (Daniel 1:8, 12). That's a quiet kind of faithfulness, friend, and I think it's the kind that gets the job done. Standing firm and being kind can ride in the same box.

And here's the part I love. Daniel didn't pull off the results himself. The text says the four looked healthier, and that "God gave knowledge and understanding" to all of them (Daniel 1:15, 17). So the win was never about vegetables, friend. It was about a God who stays with His people even in a place that isn't home, and I'm living proof that He reaches into strange places. Make up your mind, bake it in, and let Him handle the rest.
